The LOGOS build tool

Usage: largo [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  new          Create a new LOGOS project in a new directory
  init         Initialize a LOGOS project in the current directory
  build        Build the current project
  verify       Run Z3 static verification without building
  run          Build and run the current project
  serve        Serve the project over HTTP
  check        Check the project for errors without producing a binary
  opts         Report which optimizations actually fire when compiling a LOGOS file
  publish      Publish the package to the LOGOS registry
  login        Authenticate with the package registry
  logout       Remove stored credentials for a registry
  doctor       Diagnose the environment largo runs in
  repl         Start the interactive LOGOS REPL
  sat          Solve a DIMACS CNF with the certified SAT engine
  prove        Prove the theorems in a LOGOS source file (kernel-certified)
  logic        Translate English to First-Order Logic
  doc          Generate documentation from the project's `##` blocks
  add          Add a dependency to Largo.toml
  remove       Remove a dependency from Largo.toml
  fmt          Format LOGOS source files
  emit         Emit compiled code without building a binary
  bringup      Bring a model up on every chip from its one program
  expand       Show what an LGX page became: the ordinary LOGOS its constructs lower to
  clean        Remove build artifacts
  completions  Generate shell completions for largo
  replay       Re-execute a `.replay` failure artifact
  explain      Explain a diagnostic code or a language construct, offline
  mcp          Serve the LOGOS toolchain over the Model Context Protocol (stdio)
  test         Run the project's `## Test` blocks
  dap          Debug a LOGOS program over the Debug Adapter Protocol (stdio)
  lean         Lean 4 → LOGOS: import a Lean declaration as a checked LOGOS package
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
